title: Hero 'Taxes & deductions' chip shows the uncapped total, so it disagrees with the Breakdown and with Gross − Take-home whenever flat deductions exceed gross
where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:3487 (chip reads calc.ded); computeNet 1231-1255 (ded uncapped, pre/post capped for display, flat-dollar custom withholdings never capped); Breakdown 3980-3990 (also not guarded by calc.hours>0 the way the Keep chip is)
detail: computeNet returns `ded = pretax+fica+fed+st+posttax+cw` (raw) alongside display-capped `pre`/`post` (and clamps `net` at 0). The hero chip prints `ded`; the Breakdown prints the capped rows. The skill's own invariant says the caps exist 'so Breakdown still sums' — but the hero never received the same treatment, and the flat-dollar half of `cw` is outside the cap too (line 1243 folds dollar and percent withholdings into one number, line 1247 caps only pretax/posttax). Any nurse whose pretax/posttax fields are non-zero — which a paystub scan sets automatically (applyPaystub 3376-3378) — sees this on every pay period that is empty or light.
failure: pretax $600 + posttax $25 (typical after a paystub scan), scroll to next pay period with no shifts logged yet: hero reads 'Gross $0 · Taxes & deductions –$625 · $0'. Log one 8h base shift at the default $65.15: hero reads 'Gross $521 · Taxes & deductions –$665 · $0' while 'See the full breakdown' for the same period lists Pre-tax –$481 and FICA –$40, total –$521. Same shape with a flat-dollar custom withholding: $150 'Parking' on an empty period shows 'Other withholdings –$150' under 'Gross $0'. Separately: Pre-tax $300 / Post-tax $50 with no shifts yet shows 'Projected take-home $0 · Gross $0 · Taxes & deductions –$350' while the Breakdown itself shows nothing to subtract.

Add a smoke probe: computeNet(0,{pretax:600}).dedDisp === 0 and Breakdown rows sum === gross − net when pretax > gross.

title: A blanked or garbage multiplier differential is coerced to 0×, silently pricing every shift of that type at $0
where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:1046-1047 (sanitizeData: `amount: isFinite(amt) ? amt : 0` regardless of type); 4715 (Settings multiplier NumInput with min={0}); 4016-4023 (NumInput commits `min` on an empty field); 1121 (hourlyRate: `base * diff.amount`)
detail: For a dollar-type differential, 0 is the neutral value. For a multiplier-type differential (Holiday 1.5×, Overtime 1.5×), 0 zeroes the entire hourly rate — `hourlyRate` returns base*0 and shiftGross returns only the per-hour/flat bonus. Two paths produce it: NumInput's blank→min contract commits 0 when the user clears the '×' field and blurs, and sanitizeData maps any non-finite blob value to 0 rather than to 1. Once written, 0 is a finite number so sanitizeData keeps it on every subsequent load; nothing ever repairs it.
failure: In Settings, tap the Holiday '1.5 ×' field, select-all/delete to retype, then tap elsewhere before typing (common on a phone). Holiday becomes 0×. Her Christmas 12h shift now shows '~$0' on the calendar and the hero's projected take-home drops by roughly $913 (65.15×1.5×12×0.78) with no warning; the Settings row still reads '0 ×' and looks like a value she chose.
fix: In sanitizeData's differential branch, when `type==='multiplier'` coerce non-finite or ≤0 amounts to 1 (not 0). In the Settings row, give multiplier NumInputs `min={0.1}` (or make NumInput's empty-commit revert to the last good value when a `revertOnBlank` prop is set). Add a probe: sanitizeData({differentials:{holiday:{type:'multiplier',amount:''}}}).differentials.holiday.amount === 1 and hourlyRate(50,{type:'multiplier',amount:0}) is never reached from a sanitized blob.

title: Independently rounded chips: Gross − Taxes ≠ Take-home by $1 in ~11% of pay periods; Breakdown rows drift the same way
where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:3484-3487 (hero: fmt(calc.net), fmt(calc.gross), fmt(calc.ded) each rounded separately); 3982-3987 and 4006 (Breakdown: six rows and the take-home each rounded separately); fmt at 1116
detail: `fmt` rounds each figure to whole dollars on its own, so the three hero chips are three independent roundings of gross, ded and gross−ded. Replaying the real shiftGross/computeNet formulas over 220 mixes of base/night 12h shifts at five base rates with default taxes, 24 (11%) print chips whose subtraction is off by one. With six Breakdown rows the residual can reach $3. This is the 'rounding that compounds' the lens asks about — small, but it is the arithmetic a nurse is most likely to check by hand, and the app's credibility rests on the numbers closing.
failure: Two 12h base shifts at the default $65.15/hr, default taxes: hero prints 'Gross $1,564 · Taxes & deductions –$346' over a take-home of '$1,217'. 1,564 − 346 = 1,218.
fix: Display-only: derive the chip as `Math.round(calc.gross) - Math.round(calc.net)` (and likewise give Breakdown the rounding residual on its largest row, or print cents), so the visible figures always close. No change to net/gross/ded themselves — but it changes displayed dollar text, so run the wage-core equality assertion and name this as the one intended difference.
dissent:
The mechanism is real and I reproduced the exact numbers: computeNet(1563.6, defaultTaxes) with two 12h base shifts at $65.15/hr gives gross=1563.6, ded=346.3374, net=1217.2626. fmt() independently rounds each to fmt(gross)=$1,564, fmt(ded)=$346, fmt(net)=$1,217, and indeed 1564−346=1218≠1217 as displayed. So the arithmetic claim checks out exactly.

But granting the mechanism doesn't make the described outcome a bug worth reporting. Critically, computeNet (index.html:1231-1250) computes net = gross - ded in full floating-point precision from the raw, unrounded gross and ded — it is not derived by subtracting two already-rounded whole-dollar numbers. So the underlying wage math (Invariant 3's domain: shiftGross/hourlyRate/computeNet) is exact and internally consistent; nothing compounds or drifts in the actual computation. What the finding calls a defect is that fmt() — used identically everywhere in this codebase (hero chips, Breakdown rows, YearList, etc.) — rounds each of several related, independently-meaningful currency figures to the nearest whole dollar for *display* only. That a rounded subtotal minus a rounded deduction can differ by $1 from the rounded total is an unavoidable, universal property of showing whole-dollar rounded figures for numbers that don't happen to round the same way (the same artifact appears on bank statements, invoices, and virtually every budgeting app that shows subtotal/tax/total as separately rounded whole-currency amounts). Nothing in CLAUDE.md, the wage-core invariant, or the smoke-test suite promises penny-exact (or dollar-exact) reconciliation between independently displayed chips — that's a bar the finding invents and then holds the code to. The claimed severity ("the app's credibility rests on the numbers closing") is a rhetorical overstatement of a $1 cosmetic rounding artifact in a whole-dollar display, not a wage-math correctness bug, and doesn't rise to something the owner needs to act on.

title: Pattern lab and calendar price a toggled-off differential differently
where: /home/user/705-v1/index.html:1206-1213 (patternCellShiftType resolves a 'night'/weekend cell to 'base' unless differentials[k].active); 2646 (statOf) and 2795 (calc) call shiftGross(baseRate, differentials[s.shiftType], s) with no active check; hourlyRate 1119-1124
detail: The Settings toggle dims the row and removes the chip from the Add-Shift sheet (4099), and the lab treats it as 'she doesn't get this differential' — but calc/statOf/yearMonths keep applying the amount to any shift already carrying that shiftType (logged before the toggle, imported from .ics via the questionnaire at 3184, or added by a template/quick-fill). Only the delete path (4691) warns about repricing, which implies toggling off was meant to be display-only; the lab contradicts that. Either semantics is defensible; the two surfaces holding different ones is the defect.
failure: Log Mon–Wed 12h nights this period (or .ics-import them), then toggle Night off in Settings. Hero still prices them at $75.15/hr (night amount included, +$360 gross for the period). Open Patterns → 'Mon–Wed nights' preset anchored on the same week: it prices the identical three nights at $65.15/hr and shows a take-home per paycheck ~$280 lower than the hero for the same schedule.
fix: Pick one: (a) make hourlyRate/shiftGross treat `diff.active===false` as no differential so the calendar reprices to match the lab and the dimmed row (then the delete warning applies to toggling too, and the Settings hint should say so); or (b) drop the `active()` gate in patternCellShiftType so the lab prices what the calendar prices. (a) touches wage core; (b) does not, but leaves the toggle as pure decluttering. Either way add a probe covering an inactive differential on both paths.
dissent:
Verified the code (index.html:1119-1134 shiftGross/hourlyRate, 1202-1220 patternCellShiftType/patternCellToShift, 1257-1301 patternMetrics, 2636-2650 statOf, 4089-4104 AddShiftSheet, 4689-4692 tog/del) and the described mechanism is real but the "defect" framing doesn't survive scrutiny — it's a coherent, intended design, not a cross-surface contradiction.

The codebase draws one consistent line everywhere: `active` gates whether a *brand-new* shift instance can be created/classified under a given differential; it never gates the *pricing* of a shift that already carries that shiftType. That rule holds identically in every place a new shift is produced:
- Add-Shift sheet (line 4099): `differentials` filtered by `d.active` for the chip list offered for a *new* pick.
- Pattern Lab cell classification (patternCellShiftType, 1202-1211): a generic day/night cell resolves to 'base' instead of 'night'/'weekend-eve' when the differential is inactive — deciding what a *newly generated* cell becomes.
- AddShiftSheet's own live preview (4104) and statOf/calc (2646, and calc's analogue) do NOT check `.active` when pricing a shift that already has a concrete `shiftType` — by the same rule, because that shift isn't being newly created, it's being priced as recorded.

Deleting a differential (del(), 4691) is a materially different operation: it removes the key from `differentials` entirely, so `differentials[s.shiftType]` becomes `undefined` for every shift using it — hourlyRate then falls back to base for all of them, past and future, which is exactly why only *that* path warns about repricing. Toggling `active` off leaves the key (name/amount/type) intact, so already-tagged shifts keep pricing off the same, still-present definition — consistent with the general (undisputed) behavior that editing a differential's dollar amount immediately reprices every shift already tagged with that type. That's a feature, not the bug being described.

Crucially, the Pattern Lab's readout for a preset (patternMetrics, 1257-1301) never reads or reprices the shifts already on the calendar at all — it takes no `shifts` argument and computes purely from `pattern.cells` + the anchor date, generating hypothetical fresh shifts via `patternCellToShift` for a lcm(cycle,14)-day span. Opening 'Mon–Wed nights' after logging real Mon–Wed night shifts does not touch, reference, or reprice those logged shift records — it's an independent simulation of "if this preset were applied under current settings," reusing shiftGross/computeNet for calculation-methodology parity with the hero (per the comment at 1229), not for value parity with whatever happens to already be on the calendar. `planPatternApply` (1305) only consults `shifts` to decide skip-vs-replace placement, never to reprice; applying with replace=on would regenerate those specific days from scratch and only then would the calendar/hero converge with the lab's number, which is the expected lifecycle.

So the two 'surfaces' the finding pits against each other actually agree on both of the app's real rules (active gates new-shift classification; existing shiftType instances price off the persisted, non-deleted definition regardless of active). The apparent mismatch in the walkthrough is an artifact of comparing a real, already-logged shift against an unrelated hypothetical preset simulation for the same calendar dates — not a computation disagreement over the same data. This reads as intended, load-bearing behavior (mirrored by the explicit del()-only repricing warning) rather than a genuine defect.

title: poster_key is reversible: member user_ids and the board creator's id are readable, and the salt is a public constant
where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:59-69 ("see co-members" policy + full-table grants on swap_members and swap_groups), :158 (poster_key derivation); live-verified column grants on project mnnlgcxnvodjwlhhiphq
detail: Live, `authenticated` holds SELECT on swap_members(group_id, joined_at, user_id) and swap_groups(id, name, invite_code, created_by, created_at), and the "see co-members" policy returns every member row of every group the caller is in. swap_board() derives `poster_key = substr(md5(author::text || group_id::text || 'scrubpay-swaps'), 1, 8)`. The salt is a string constant in a public repo (github.com/patrick222-dotcom/705-v1 answers `"private": false`), group_id is known to every member, and md5 is a browser one-liner. So `supabase.from('swap_members').select('user_id,joined_at').eq('group_id',G)` yields the N candidate authors; hashing each gives a complete poster_key -> user_id table for the board. Binding a uuid to a person: swap_groups.created_by names the board creator outright (the one who sent everyone the link); joined_at orders the others against who-got-the-link-when; and a single confirmed match pins uid <-> display_name permanently (reveal returns post_id -> name and that post's key was on the board). The migration comment at :155-157 says "Not reversible" and the 2026-07-30 audit checked only that the `author` column can't be selected -- nobody tested rebuilding the key from readable columns. The client never selects from swap_members (only the insert at index.html:1706) and reads only id,name,invite_code (+ order by created_at) from swap_groups (index.html:1675, 1719), so both grants are pure over-exposure.
failure: A nurse posts "give up Fri 9/19 night" after the app tells her "Posted -- your unit sees it anonymously." (index.html:5062). Any co-member with devtools runs one REST select and one md5 loop and knows which uuid posted it; if she created the board, `created_by` names her with no inference at all. Every post she makes in that group is tagged to her from then on -- the feature's core promise is false.
fix: Step 1, grants only (no key change, no client change): `revoke select, update on public.swap_members from authenticated;` (keep insert -- the client's insert at index.html:1706 sends Prefer: return=minimal, and is_swap_member/join_swap_group run as definer) and `revoke select, update on public.swap_groups from authenticated; grant select (id, name, invite_code, created_at) on public.swap_groups to authenticated;`. Step 2: stop deriving the key from a public constant -- keep a per-group random secret in a table with no grants to anon/authenticated and read it inside swap_board (definer), so a leaked uid can never be turned into a key. Nothing persists poster_key client-side (it is recomputed from each board fetch), so changing the derivation has no data impact. Add two probes to the RLS audit: as member A, `select user_id from swap_members` must be 403; `select created_by from swap_groups` must be 403.

title: propose_swap never checks the caller is a leg: any member can reserve and hide any two posts on the board
where: supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:245-265 (propose_swap); live pg_get_functiondef is identical
detail: The RPC validates membership, 2-3 legs, and that each post is open and in the group -- but never that auth.uid() authors any of the legs. The only thing keeping proposals to "matches involving me" is the client: computeSwapSuggestions (index.html:1763-1835) only emits suggestions with a 'me' leg and doPropose (index.html:5079-5099) passes them through. Any member can call `supabase.rpc('propose_swap',{g, post_ids:[x,y]})` with any two open post ids returned by swap_board. Each call flips both posts to 'proposed': swap_board (:164) then hides them from everyone but their authors, openPosts (index.html:5302) drops them, and computeSwapSuggestions ignores them; the two authors get a "WAITING ON 2 OF 2 TO ACCEPT" card pairing them with a stranger's unrelated post. The proposer is not a party, so they can neither see nor decline it -- only the victims can (decline_swap_match) -- and the attacker re-proposes on the next 15s poll. No rate limit, no per-user cap on open matches, and status 'expired' exists but nothing ever sets it.
failure: One member with the invite code pairs every open post on the board in a loop from the console: the board reads "Nothing posted yet" for the whole unit and every poster is stuck declining nonsense matches that come straight back. Selectively: lock every other 'give' for Friday so only their own remains visible to the colleague who wants it.
fix: In propose_swap, after the foreach loop and before `return m`: `if not exists (select 1 from swap_match_legs where match_id = m and leg_user = auth.uid()) then raise exception 'not_a_party'; end if;` -- the exception rolls back the match, legs and status flips. Optionally cap concurrent 'proposed' matches per proposer (e.g. 5) in the same function. Add an audit probe: as member C, propose posts by A and B only -> must raise not_a_party and leave both posts 'open'.

title: MAX_BLOB_BYTES is enforced only in the browser; user_data.data has no server-side size bound, so one signed-in account can fill the shared free-tier database
where: supabase/migrations/000_core.sql:27 (data jsonb, no CHECK); confirmed live via pg_constraint — user_data carries only PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY and UNIQUE(user_id), no trigger. Client side: index.html:2464 (the only size check), index.html:2496 (pagehide flush) and index.html:2512 (retrySync) call saveToSupabase without it; saveToSupabase itself at index.html:1324-1344 does no size check.
detail: The 512KB cap that CLAUDE.md calls the 'free-tier guard' is a JavaScript comparison in the debounced save effect. The table has no `pg_column_size(data)` CHECK (compare `events.props`, which does have one in the same migration), and RLS only constrains *which row* an authenticated user may write, not *how big*. Since the Google OAuth app is In production, any Google account is a valid `authenticated` caller against the public anon key. Even inside the app the cap is not actually held: when the debounce path trips it, it toasts 'cloud sync paused' and returns, but the `pagehide`/`visibilitychange` flush (2496) and the manual retry (2512) both call saveToSupabase directly with the same oversized `snapshotRef`/`serializeState()` and write it anyway. Separately, the check compares `JSON.stringify(...).length` (UTF-16 code units) against a byte budget, so non-ASCII notes can be ~3x the intended bytes before it trips.
failure: A hostile (or merely curious) signed-in user issues `POST /rest/v1/user_data` (Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates, on_conflict=user_id) with the public anon key + their own JWT and `data` = tens of MB of random base64 (incompressible, so TOAST does not shrink it), repeating the update to leave dead tuples behind. Nothing in Postgres refuses it. The free-tier project crosses its 500MB database quota and Supabase drops it to read-only: every other user's `saveToSupabase` then fails on every edit, each device falls into the failed-save backup mode with the sync-error badge, and cross-device sync stops for everyone until the owner intervenes in the dashboard. In-app variant a real user would see: after the 'cloud sync paused' toast, backgrounding the tab silently uploads the oversized blob the toast just said was not being uploaded.
fix: Add migration 004 (000 is never back-edited): `alter table public.user_data add constraint user_data_data_size check (pg_column_size(data) <= 524288), add constraint user_data_data_is_object check (jsonb_typeof(data) = 'object');` — matches the pattern already used for `events.props`. Then move the size check into `saveToSupabase` itself (return null and logClientError when `new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(data)).length > MAX_BLOB_BYTES`) so the flush and retry paths share it, and treat a 23514 from the server like any other failed save (backup + syncError), which the existing branch already does.

title: Hero's 'See the full breakdown' / 'Share BadgeBudget' links accidentally inherit the full .hero card style, ballooning them and adding dead scroll space to the very first screen
where: index.html:3491-3492 (className="hero more linklike"); CSS: .linklike padding:0 at 79, .hero padding/border-radius/background/box-shadow at 114, .hero .more at 119
detail: The two footer buttons are given className="hero more linklike" — three independent classes, not a scoped ".hero .more" selector. Because the token "hero" is also the class name of the enclosing card, both buttons literally match the top-level `.hero{background:var(--ink);border-radius:22px;padding:22px 24px;...box-shadow:...}` rule (line 114) in addition to `.hero .more` (119) and `.linklike` (79). `.hero` and `.linklike` have equal CSS specificity (one class each), so the tie is broken by source order, and `.hero` (declared later, at line 114) beats `.linklike`'s `padding:0` (line 79) — the buttons keep `.hero`'s 22px/24px padding, border-radius and box-shadow instead of being flush, padding-free text links. Verified live on an iPhone-13 viewport: document.querySelectorAll('.hero') genuinely returns 3 elements (the card plus both buttons); each button's computed style is 'padding: 22px 24px', height balloons to 59px, and a screenshot shows each rendering as its own visible dark rounded pill with an inset highlight seam nested inside the real hero card, rather than a plain link line.
failure: On every load, the hero card — the first thing a nurse sees, and the thing the whole app is built around — is roughly 120px taller than intended, almost entirely padding around two one-line links. One-handed on a phone, that's extra scrolling distance before she reaches the calendar / '+ Log a shift' controls beneath it, and the two links visually read as broken/unstyled boxes rather than the intended small footer actions.
fix: Stop reusing the literal token "hero" as a class on these buttons — give them a distinct class (e.g. "hero-more") so they no longer match the card-level .hero rule, or restructure so the descendant relationship is expressed purely through DOM nesting rather than a repeated class name.

title: Overtime tag text fails AA contrast in the Add-Shift live preview and shift list
where: index.html:4197 and index.html:4245 (color '#11A86B' inline overrides; also the decorative badge at 3923 and legend swatch text-adjacent use at 4218 share the same token)
detail: The 'OT ×1.5' annotation is rendered with inline color:'#11A86B' (var(--money)). At line 4197 it sits on the 'ON THIS DAY' row list's white background (.row-item{background:#fff}, line 421) — measured contrast 3.07:1. At line 4245 it sits on the live preview's mint-tinted panel (.preview{background:var(--money-soft)}, line 418) — measured contrast 2.75:1. Both are far under the 4.5:1 WCAG AA minimum for normal-weight text this size (12-12.5px, not 'large text' under WCAG's 14pt-bold/18pt threshold). failure: A low-vision nurse comparing 'is this shift worth picking up because of the OT multiplier' sees a washed-out, hard-to-read 'OT ×1.5' tag right next to the dollar amount that explains why the number is higher than a normal shift — exactly the moment this app is built to make legible.

title: Pay-period stepper's scroll animation ignores prefers-reduced-motion
where: animateScrollTop (index.html:674-683), used by scrollFocusToDate (index.html:2751-2766) via movePeriod (index.html:2826-2831)
detail: The ‹/› pay-period stepper in the greet row calls movePeriod, which calls scrollFocusToDate, which drives the calendar's scroll position with animateScrollTop — a hand-rolled requestAnimationFrame loop that eases el.scrollTop over 380ms. This is plain JS, not a CSS transition/animation. The file's own reduced-motion rule (index.html:469-471, `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){ *{animation-duration:.001ms!important;transition-duration:.001ms!important;scroll-behavior:auto!important} }`) only collapses CSS-driven durations and `scroll-behavior` (native smooth-scroll); it has no effect on a loop that sets `el.scrollTop` directly on every rAF frame. There is no `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` check anywhere in the file (confirmed via grep).
failure: A user with 'reduce motion' enabled at the OS level taps › next to the pay-period label while in Month view. The entire calendar viewport still animates a smooth 380ms scroll to the new period's position — exactly the kind of scrolling motion the reduced-motion setting exists to suppress, and exactly the kind of thing this same file is careful to suppress for boot timers/CSS transitions elsewhere.
fix: Check `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` at the top of animateScrollTop (or in scrollFocusToDate before calling it) and jump `el.scrollTop = clamped` synchronously instead of animating when the user has that preference set.

title: Add-Shift sheet has no dialog semantics, unlike every sibling sheet in the same file
where: index.html:4164 (AddShiftSheet's outer <div className="sheet">)
detail: Every other modal sheet in the app declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="..." on its .sheet element: the feedback sheet (line 2057, aria-label="Send feedback"), the .ics import-confirm sheet (3820, "Confirm schedule import"), the classify-imported-shift sheet (3848, "Classify imported shift"), and both swap sheets (5311/5330, "Shift swaps"). AddShiftSheet's own <div className="sheet"> at 4164 carries none of these. failure: A screen-reader user who opens 'Add a shift' from a calendar day gets no announcement that a dialog named 'Add a shift' just opened, and the assistive-tech virtual cursor is free to wander into the calendar/dashboard behind the scrim while it is nominally modal — the exact opposite of what happens one sheet over (Import/Classify/Feedback/Swaps) for the identical visual pattern. title: Pattern Lab's dialog has no dialog role, no aria-modal, and no accessible name — unlike every sibling sheet

title: Pattern Lab has no focus trap and no Escape-to-close, so keyboard focus leaks into the obscured app behind it
where: index.html:4300-4581 (function PatternLab, no keydown handling or focus management anywhere in the component); index.html:2596-2600 (body-scroll lock is the only 'modal open' side effect); index.html:1966-1968 (Escape-to-close exists for the account menu, for contrast)
detail: There is no `useEffect`/`addEventListener('keydown', ...)` and no ref-based focus trap anywhere in PatternLab (confirmed by reading lines 4300-4420 and grepping the whole component body). The app never uses `ReactDOM.createPortal` (grep returns nothing) and never sets `inert` or toggles `aria-hidden` on background content when a sheet opens — the only 'a modal is open' side effect anywhere in the app is `document.body.style.overflow='hidden'` at line 2598, which blocks page scroll but does nothing to the DOM's tab order or accessibility tree. failure: A keyboard user opens Pattern Lab, then presses Shift+Tab from the '×' Close button (aria-label="Close", line 4419) — focus moves backward into whatever topnav/calendar control precedes PatternLab in the DOM (e.g. the 'Patterns'/'Swaps'/'Settings' topnav links or a calendar day cell), all of which are still fully interactive but visually hidden under the `.scrim` overlay (`rgba(18,18,26,.55)` + blur, line 394). title: Onboarding step transitions never move focus and use no heading markup

The 'high' severity is also overstated for a linear 5-step wizard with a visible progress bar and no branching, where AT users still encounter new content via normal tab/swipe navigation; this is degraded UX, not a broken/inaccessible flow. title: pagehide/visibilitychange flush silently drops an edit when the best-effort save fails
where: index.html:2489-2505 (flush), contrast with the debounced save effect's failure handling at index.html:2470-2479; saveToSupabase at index.html:1324-1344
detail: The debounced save effect explicitly guards against a failed cloud write: when saveToSupabase(...) resolves null (it always resolves, never throws — see the catch at 1339-1343 and the error branch at 1337), the else branch at line 2478 calls writeBackup(user.id, dataToSave) so the edit survives locally under BACKUP_KEY. The separate `flush` handler registered for `pagehide`/`visibilitychange`→hidden (added specifically because '500ms debounce would otherwise drop it', per the comment at 2489) does not do this: its call chain is `saveToSupabase(...).then(ts=>{ if(ts){ ...clear backup... } })` — the `if(ts)` guard only handles the success path. When `ts` is null/falsy (network drop, RLS/Postgres error, or the fetch simply being torn down mid-flight as the page actually unloads), the `.then` body does nothing: no writeBackup call, no error surfaced.
failure: Signed-in user edits a shift, then immediately backgrounds or closes the tab (the debounce hasn't fired yet, which is exactly the case this handler exists for) on a flaky connection. The pagehide-triggered save fails; because flush's failure branch is a no-op, the edit is written to BACKUP_KEY nowhere, never reaches Supabase, and — once the tab is actually gone — no longer exists in memory either. On the next load, hydrateFromCloud finds no newer backup and no newer cloud row, so the edit is gone with no toast, no syncError, and no recovery path, unlike every other save-failure path in the app.
fix: Mirror the debounced effect's failure handling in flush: when saveToSupabase resolves falsy, call writeBackup(snap.user.id, snap.data) just like line 2478 does. Because a `.then()` callback isn't guaranteed to run once actual page teardown begins, prefer writing the backup synchronously before firing the best-effort save (optimistic backup, cleared only on confirmed success) rather than only in the async continuation.
dissent: The asymmetry the finding describes is real (index.html:2496 has no writeBackup on a null result; 2478 does) and it is not in the KNOWN list or BACKLOG.md. But it is not a data-loss defect of the shape or severity claimed. (1) The flush is layered on top of the debounced save, not a replacement for it: on visibilitychange→hidden the 500ms timer at 2452 is still pending and is not cancelled. On desktop it fires within ~1s (throttled); on iOS it fires the moment the tab is foregrounded again. That path then does the full failure handling — writeBackup + setSyncError(true) — so the "no toast, no syncError, no recovery" claim is false for every background-and-return case, which is the common phone gesture. The edit is only unrecoverable if the OS discards the suspended tab before it is ever resumed, on top of a failed network write, on top of the edit having landed in the final 500ms. (2) On real pagehide (tab closed), the `.then` continuation is precisely the code that is not guaranteed to run during teardown — the finding concedes this — so adding an else-branch there does not close the window; the flush is explicitly best-effort ("best-effort immediate cloud save", 2495) and when it fails the user is exactly where they would be with no flush at all: the last <500ms edit before closing is lost. That is the pre-existing, inherent limit of a 500ms debounce, not a regression introduced by the flush handler "dropping" anything. (3) The remaining fix — an optimistic synchronous backup before every flush — changes the documented meaning of BACKUP_KEY ("written ONLY when a cloud save fails, so it always holds work the cloud never received", 2270-2272) on the hydrate path that once ate 47 days of shifts; it is a small hardening idea, not a high-severity integrity bug, and not something to schedule on the strength of a narrowed-down last-half-second-offline-then-discarded scenario. At most a P3 note for a dedicated sync session, if ever.

title: Manual sign-out doesn't mirror the SIGNED_OUT cleanup it claims to, leaking the previous user's iCal credential into the next sign-in
where: index.html:2528-2538 (handleSignOut) vs index.html:2409-2419 (onAuthStateChange SIGNED_OUT branch)
detail: onAuthStateChange's else-branch (2409-2419) resets several things on sign-out including, per its own comment 'Drop the signed-in user's calendar subscription from memory (never leak it to anon state)': setHydratedUserId(null), setIcalSub(null), setIcalUrl(''), icalSyncedForUser.current=null. handleSignOut (the only call site is the account-menu Sign out button, wired at line 3450) is commented 'Mirrors the SIGNED_OUT branch (safe/idempotent if that also fires)' and exists specifically because signOut() can deadlock on iOS WebKit so onAuthStateChange may never fire (same bug the getSession 4s-race guards, per the comment at 2518-2521). But its own reset block (2533-2536) only touches hydratedForUser.current/lastSeenAt.current/prevUserId.current/setSyncError/setSession/setUser/resetToDefaults() — it omits all four iCal statements. In the exact WebKit-deadlock case this function was written for, onAuthStateChange never runs, so nothing clears hydratedUserId/icalSub/icalUrl/icalSyncedForUser.current. resetToDefaults() itself (2335-2340) also doesn't touch them; that state lives only in the two places above, and the Settings sheet's calendar-sync input is bound directly to icalUrl (index.html:4790) plus icalSub.lastSynced (4800-4801).
failure: Two nurses share one phone (the app's own documented sharing model — a QR handed over 'off Courtney's screen'). Nurse A signs out on iOS Safari during a WebKit signOut() deadlock (handleSignOut times out via withTimeout, purges the auth token, but onAuthStateChange's cleanup never fires). React state still holds A's icalUrl/icalSub/hydratedUserId. Nurse B then signs in on the same phone. onAuthStateChange sets user=B immediately, so Settings' `{user && <CALENDAR SYNC>}` block (index.html:4781-4802) renders right away — showing A's still-resident icalUrl (a bearer credential per Invariant 13, 'treat the link like a password') in B's Settings until the async loadIcalSub(B.id) resolves and overwrites it a network round-trip later.
fix: Add the same four lines handleSignOut is missing — setHydratedUserId(null); setIcalSub(null); setIcalUrl(''); icalSyncedForUser.current=null; — to handleSignOut's reset block, or factor both cleanup blocks into one shared function so they can't diverge again.

where: resetToDefaults() index.html:2335-2340 (called from the auth-state-change SIGNED_OUT branch at 2414 and from handleSignOut at 2536); obStep state at 2192-2201; finish() at 3408-3414; Onboarding done screen at 5812-5834

On SIGNED_OUT, resetToDefaults() sets setupComplete=false, and in the very same handler a setTimeout(0) immediately re-applies the previous anonymous localStorage blob via applyData(...,{landCurrent:true}), which sets setupComplete back from that data (true for any anon user who'd used the app before signing in). title: pagehide/visibility flush silently drops a failed cloud save (no backup, no error surfaced)
where: index.html:2489-2505 (the `flush` effect), contrast with the debounced-save effect at 2470-2479
detail: The main debounced save path (2470-2479) treats `saveToSupabase`'s return value as significant on both branches: on success it updates `lastSeenAt` and clears the backup key, on failure (`ts` falsy) it calls `writeBackup(user.id, dataToSave)` and `setSyncError(true)`. The `flush()` handler, which exists specifically to catch the last edit before the tab is backgrounded or closed ('the 500ms debounce would otherwise drop it', comment at 2489), only wires up the success case: `saveToSupabase(snap.user.id, snap.data).then(ts=>{ if(ts){ lastSeenAt.current=ts; ...removeItem... } })` (line 2496). There is no `else` and no `.catch()` — if `ts` is null (RLS error, dropped network request, Supabase 5xx), nothing happens: `writeBackup` is never called and `syncError` is never set.
failure: A nurse edits a shift, then immediately backgrounds the app (switches apps / locks the phone) — exactly the moment this handler is designed for. If that cloud write happens to fail (a very plausible time for a mobile network hiccup), the edit is not persisted to Supabase, not written to the per-user failed-save backup (`nursingWagePlannerData::<uid>`), and no sync-error indicator is shown. If the tab is actually killed (not just backgrounded) rather than resumed, that edit is gone with no trace and no recovery path, even though Invariant 4's whole 'per-user failed-save backup... wins when newer than the cloud row' mechanism exists precisely to prevent this class of loss.
fix: Give the flush handler the same failure branch as the debounced-save effect: on `ts` falsy, call `writeBackup(snap.user.id, snap.data)` (and ideally `setSyncError(true)`, though a state update racing tab teardown is less critical than the local backup write).

title: Hero's "Taxes & deductions" chip can show a bigger deduction than the gross next to it, and disagrees with the Breakdown a tap away
where: index.html:3487 (hero chip renders calc.ded) and index.html:1244-1250 (computeNet)
detail: computeNet() computes `ded = pretax+fica+fed+st+posttax+cw` uncapped (line 1244) and returns it as `ded`, but then deliberately caps the *displayed* pre/post fields (`dispPre`/`dispPost`, lines 1246-1249) specifically 'so Breakdown rows still sum' when a period's gross can't absorb the full flat pretax/posttax deductions. The hero's chip at line 3487 (`Taxes & deductions –{fmt(calc.ded)}`) is the one and only other consumer of `.ded` in the whole file (confirmed by grep) and uses the raw uncapped value, so it never got the same treatment.
failure: Any signed-in nurse who has entered a per-period Pre-tax or Post-tax deduction in Settings (a completely normal, first-class field, not an edge feature) and views a pay period where she hasn't logged shifts yet -- the default state at the start of every new two-week period, or right after finishing Settings before adding a single shift -- sees a hero that reads e.g. 'Projected take-home $0' with chips 'Gross $0' next to 'Taxes & deductions –$260' (reproduced exactly: pretaxDeductions=200, posttaxDeductions=60, gross=0 -> ded=260, net=0). title: "Take-home per paycheck" is a cycle-average, shown with full confidence, for the exact rotations where real paychecks diverge from it
where: patternMetrics index.html:1257-1299 (comment at 1253-1256); displayed unqualified in PatternLab at index.html:4428 (compare table), 4447 (pattern card), 4540-4542 (edit-mode money block)
detail: patternMetrics averages gross/net over lcm(cycle,14) days and divides by (span/14) periods to get periodGross/periodNet/periodHours (1294-1298). The average of a real 14-day paycheck window over a periodic on/off sequence is invariant to which phase of the cycle a given real paycheck lands on ONLY when the cycle length divides 14 evenly (i.e. cycle ∈ {2,7,14} within the allowed 2..42 range) — because only then does every non-overlapping 14-day window contain the same whole number of full cycles. For every other cycle length — which includes the built-in 'weekend'-adjacent choice of 28 days in PATTERN_CYCLE_CHOICES (1146) and, most visibly, the shipped preset '4 on, 4 off nights' (id 4on4off, cycle:8, index.html:1163-1164) — consecutive real 14-day paychecks contain a DIFFERENT number of actual shifts depending on where the cycle's phase falls, so the true paychecks alternate above and below the displayed average rather than matching it. Concretely, for the 4on4off preset with the app's own default baseRate 65.15 and night differential +10 (index.html:2204, 688), a 12h night shift grosses 75.15*12=$901.80 (shiftGross, 1125-1133). Over the lcm(8,14)=56-day span (4 periods) the real per-period shift counts are 8,8,6,6 (28 total, matching 7 cycles * 4 shifts/cycle) — i.e. real paychecks alternate between ≈$7,214 and ≈$5,411 gross (a ~$1,800 swing), while the lab shows one flat number: the average of those, ≈$6,313. Every actual paycheck a nurse who applies this pattern receives will be either noticeably higher or noticeably lower than the number she was shown before committing to the rotation — exactly the kind of surprise the app's whole premise ("know what a shift is worth before it's worked") exists to prevent. The code's own comment at 1254-1256 calls this averaging 'an honest per-paycheck figure,' but nothing in the UI tells the user it's an average: the yearly figure is explicitly hedged with '≈' (line 4542, '≈ {fmt(metrics.yearNet)} a year') while the much more decision-relevant per-paycheck figure right next to it, and in the pattern list card and side-by-side comparison table, carries no such hedge anywhere.
failure: A nurse opens Pattern lab, picks the built-in '4 on, 4 off nights' preset (or types a custom 28-day cycle), sees 'Take-home per paycheck: $X' with no qualifier, and applies it to her calendar planning around that number. Her first real paycheck comes in ~$900-1,800 different (net) from what she was shown, with no warning that the number she budgeted against was ever anything but a fixed promise for every check.
fix: Qualify periodNet/periodGross/periodHours the same way yearNet already is — at minimum prefix them with '≈' in all three surfaces (index.html:4428, 4447, 4540-4542) whenever metrics.drifts is true or, more precisely, whenever cycle length doesn't evenly divide 14, and add one line under the money block naming that real paychecks will alternate (e.g. 'averaged — cycles that don't line up with a 2-week pay period pay more some checks and less others'). This is a display-only change in PatternLab and doesn't require touching patternMetrics's math, though a stronger fix (surfacing the actual min/max per-period swing) would.

title: Welcome-screen sample take-home figure is hardcoded and doesn't match the app's own math for the identical schedule
where: index.html:5721-5722 (welcome screen literal) vs sampleNet() at index.html:3416-3423, DIFF_DEFAULTS at index.html:686-697, default baseRate at index.html:2204
detail:
The obStep===0 welcome screen shows a static, non-computed figure: `
Sample · 72 hrs this period
` followed by `
$3,951
` (line 5721-5722) — literal strings, not derived from any function. The same '72 hrs / 6 shifts' scenario is independently defined a few hundred lines later in `sampleNet()` (3 night + 2 weekend-day + 1 base, 12h each = 72 hrs), which the 'done' screen (obStep 4) actually renders via `fmt(sample.net)`. Computing sampleNet() by hand with the app's current defaults (baseRate=65.15 at line 2204, DIFF_DEFAULTS night=+$10/hr and weekend-day=+$11.5/hr at line 686, federal 12%, state 2.5%, FICA standard 7.65%, no pretax/posttax) gives gross = 3*(75.15*12) + 2*(76.65*12) + 1*(65.15*12) = 5326.80, and net = 5326.80 - (5326.80*0.0765 + 5326.80*0.12 + 5326.80*0.025) = 5326.80 - 1180.04 = 4146.76, i.e. fmt() would show $4,147 — not $3,951. The two numbers disagree by about $196 (≈5%) for what is presented as the exact same 72-hour, 6-shift schedule.
failure: A brand-new visitor sees '$3,951' on the very first screen (framed as 'we do the messy math so the number's never a surprise'). If she continues through the full setup path (steps 1-3) without touching any rate, the 'done' screen a few taps later — using the same default rate and the same 72-hour/6-shift assumption — shows $4,147 instead. The app contradicts its own headline number within a single onboarding session, which is precisely the kind of surprise the product claims to eliminate.
fix: Either compute the welcome-screen figure the same way sampleNet() does (call the existing sampleNet-equivalent logic against current default state, which is already in scope at obStep 0) so the two screens can never drift apart again, or replace the literal '$3,951' with a value that is verified to match sampleNet()'s output under the current defaults. Do not hand-tune the string again without re-deriving it — that is how it went stale.

title: "Clear the sample" removes the seeded shifts but leaves the placeholder $65.15/hr rate in place with no indication it isn't real, once the honesty banner is gone
where: index.html:2991-3000 (clearSample), index.html:3408-3412 (finish('sample')), index.html:2231 and 969 (estimateMode is the only signal that the rate is fake)
detail: finish('sample') (line 3408-3412) sets `baseRate` to the placeholder 65.15 and seeds sample shifts, marking the state as fake only via `estimateMode:'sample'`. The est-banner (line 3464-3475) offers two exits when estimateMode==='sample': 'Enter my rate' (opens Settings) and 'Clear the sample' (calls `clearSample`). `clearSample` (line 2991-3000) strips the SAMPLE_PATTERN_ID-tagged shifts and unconditionally does `setEstimateMode('')` — it never checks whether the user actually entered a real base rate first. There is no other field anywhere (grep confirms `estimateMode` is the sole indicator) distinguishing 'nurse's real $65.15/hr' from 'never-touched placeholder $65.15/hr'.
failure: A nurse taps 'Show me an example' to see how the app works, then taps 'Clear the sample' directly (never 'Enter my rate'). The seeded shifts vanish and the banner disappears — but baseRate is still the fictitious 65.15. Every shift she now logs herself computes gross/take-home/hero figures against that fake rate with no banner, no warning, and nothing in the UI distinguishing it from a confirmed real rate. This state also serializes into the cloud blob and localStorage (serializeState includes baseRate and estimateMode='' ), so it persists across sessions and devices silently. The app's headline numbers are now systematically wrong for her actual pay, with the one mechanism designed to flag that (the est-banner) already dismissed.
fix: Track whether the base rate was ever explicitly set by the user (independent of estimateMode), or make `clearSample` refuse/redirect to rate entry when `baseRate` still equals the untouched sample default, so clearing the sample can never silently promote a placeholder rate to authoritative status.

title: Editing a savings goal's target down to $0 in Settings makes the Add-Shift preview show "Infinity%"
where: index.html:4248 (AddShiftSheet preview) / index.html:4686 & 4754 (Settings updGoalTarget + NumInput)
detail:
In Settings' SAVINGS GOALS list, each goal's target is edited with `<NumInput value={g.target} onCommit={v=>updGoalTarget(g.id,v)} min={0} .../>` (index.html:4754), and `updGoalTarget=(id,v)=>setGoals((goals||[]).map(g=> g.id===id ? {...g, target:parseFloat(v)||0} : g))` (index.html:4686) has no floor above 0. NumInput's own commit logic (index.html:4020-4028) sets the value to `min` (i.e. 0) whenever the field is cleared and blurred, or the user simply types 0. So a goal that already exists with a positive target can be driven to `target:0` entirely from the UI, live, in the same session — no reload and no pass through `sanitizeData` in between (Settings and AddShiftSheet share the exact same top-level `goals` state, wired at index.html:3617 and index.html:4677).

The forward per-shift preview at index.html:4247-4248 computes `const pct=Math.round(previewNet/g.target*1000)/10; const n=Math.ceil(g.target/previewNet);` guarded only by `previewNet>0` — there is no `g.target>0` check here (unlike the Settings reverse-view at index.html:4748, which does guard with `per>0 && g.target>0`, and unlike `sanitizeData`'s goals filter at index.html:1069-1081, which explicitly drops any goal whose `target` isn't a finite positive number specifically "so a malformed value can't yield NaN percentages in the shift preview"). With `g.target===0`, `previewNet/g.target` is `Infinity` in JS (positive/0), so `pct` is `Infinity` and the template literal renders the literal string "Infinity%".
failure: 1) Open Settings → SAVINGS GOALS, tap into an existing goal's amount field, clear it (or type 0) and tap/tab away so it blurs — the goal's target silently becomes $0, with no error or warning. 2) Close Settings and open the Add-Shift sheet for any day with a shift that has nonzero take-home. The goal line at the bottom of the shift preview reads e.g. "toward your goal: House down payment Infinity% (≈0 shifts)" — a glaringly broken, alarming figure shown right next to the take-home dollar amount the app exists to make trustworthy.
fix: Guard the AddShiftSheet goal line the same way the Settings reverse view already does — skip (or filter out) any goal whose `target` is not finite and > 0, e.g. change the `.map` at index.html:4248 to filter `goals.filter(g=>g.target>0)` before computing pct/n, or add `g.target>0 &&` inside the per-goal computation. Ideally also stop `updGoalTarget` from ever committing a non-positive target in the first place (e.g. clamp to the previous value, or require target>0 the same way `addGoal` already does at index.html:4684-4685), since that closes the root cause rather than just the one downstream symptom.

title: Swap board lets a nurse commit to a shift with zero indication of what it pays
where: index.html:3643 (SwapsSheet call site), 4819 (SwapsSheet signature), 5505-5531 (SUGGESTED FOR YOU cards), 5079-5099 (doPropose), 4067-4072 (giveMetaLine)
detail:
SwapsSheet is invoked at index.html:3643 with `user, shifts, dayEvents, notes, saveDayShifts, differentials` — no `baseRate`, no `keepRatio`, no tax inputs. Compare the sibling sheets at the same call-site block: AddShiftSheet gets `baseRate={baseRate} keepRatio={keepRatio}` and PatternLab gets `baseRate={baseRate} taxes={taxInputs}`. SwapsSheet structurally cannot compute a dollar figure for anything it shows, because it was never given the numbers to do it with. Its own comment at giveMetaLine (4066: "wage-free by construction — shift_meta never carries $") makes this deliberate for the *data model* (correct: differing bonus/OT status shouldn't transfer between nurses), but it also blocks the client-side display, which has nothing to do with the anonymity model and could safely use the viewer's own baseRate/differentials the same way AddShiftSheet already does (previewGross/previewNet at 4104-4105).
The result: the 'SUGGESTED FOR YOU' cards (5505-5531) render PICK UP / TRADE / 3-WAY SHUFFLE suggestions as date + shift-type + hours only (`describeLeg`, 5509) and a bare 'Propose' button (5527) that calls doPropose (5079) straight into `proposeSwapMatch`, which freezes the posts. Nothing between seeing the suggestion and committing to it ever calls `shiftGross`/`computeNet` on the incoming shift.
failure: A nurse opens Swaps, sees 'PICK UP · Fri Sep 19 · Night ×12h' and taps Propose. Once the other party accepts, the match is confirmed and effectively irreversible except through a Decline that the app itself frames as a social cost ('The others involved will see it fell through', 5155). Only after fully committing — accepting, revealing names, and tapping 'Add to my calendar' (doApplyPlan, 5260) — does she discover, via the Planner hero, what that shift actually pays. She had no way to compare this pickup against staying home, or against another posted shift, before agreeing to it. This directly contradicts the app's own stated promise, verbatim at the welcome screen ('Know your real take-home before you pick up the shift', line 5718) and the share blurb ('see what a shift is really worth before you pick it up', line 5667) — and it's inconsistent with the app's own established convention of surfacing $/hr specifically to 'compare pickups at a glance' (AddShiftSheet, line 4246), a convention the swap board's literal 'PICK UP' feature doesn't follow.
fix: Pass `baseRate` and `keepRatio` (or the fuller `taxes`, matching PatternLab) into SwapsSheet, and render an estimated take-home (or at minimum ≈$/hr) on each suggestion card and open board post using the viewer's own rate — the same `shiftGross`/`computeNet` calls AddShiftSheet already makes, applied to `shift_meta` — before the Propose button, not after acceptance. This adds a new displayed dollar figure, so it should go through the wage-core protocol (baseline probes, a new assertion, the deployed-build equality check) even though it doesn't touch shiftGross/computeNet/calc themselves — flagging wageCore for that reason.

title: privacy.html misdescribes sign-in as Google-only and claims no password is ever stored, but email/password is the app's primary, first-shown auth path
where: privacy.html:89-91 ("Your account" section) vs index.html:4584-4671 (AuthModal), specifically handleEmailAuth at index.html:4591-4613
detail: privacy.html says: "Sign-in uses Google. BadgeBudget receives your email address and name from Google and stores no password." But AuthModal (index.html:4584) renders an email+password form (the <form onSubmit={handleEmailAuth}> block, index.html:4638-4651) ABOVE the "or" divider, with "Continue with Google" as the secondary option below it (index.html:4658-4661). handleEmailAuth calls supabase.auth.signUp({email,password}) or supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({email,password}) (index.html:4600-4602) -- Supabase Auth stores a (hashed) password for every such account. `git log -S"signInWithPassword"` shows this path was added 2026-08-23 (PR #45), three weeks before privacy.html was written/last-updated 2026-09-07 (PR #78), so this isn't stale copy that predates the feature -- the notice was written after the feature existed and still doesn't mention it.
failure: A nurse who reads privacy.html before signing up, sees 'stores no password', and then creates an account via the email+password form (the first, more prominent option in the modal) has just had a password stored by the service, contradicting what she was told. She also isn't told BadgeBudget/Supabase directly receives and stores the email address she typed (the notice frames email receipt as something that only happens 'from Google'). This is a factual misstatement about data handling on the one page whose job is to state that accurately, and the same page backs the Google OAuth consent screen the owner is trying to get brand-verified.
fix: Update the "Your account" section of privacy.html to disclose both auth paths: e.g. "Sign-in uses Google OAuth or email/password, your choice. With Google, BadgeBudget receives your email address and name and stores no password. With email/password, your password is stored (hashed) by the auth provider (Supabase) -- BadgeBudget's own code never sees or stores it in plain text." No app-code change needed; this is a documentation-accuracy fix, not a wage-core or telemetry-code change.

title: Add-Shift preview, calendar day cells, goal lines and the weekend-night card use a keep-ratio that omits percent custom withholdings, so they disagree with the hero and the pattern lab
where: index.html:2819-2820 (keepRatio) -> consumers at 4104-4105 & 4245-4248 (AddShiftSheet preview + goal line), 3919 & 3933 (Calendar day cell), 4747 (Settings '≈ N typical 12h shifts'), 3434 & 3512 ('Pick up a weekend night?' card)
detail: The hero (calc, 2787-2810) and the pattern lab (patternMetrics 1298) both price take-home through computeNet(), which subtracts customWithholdings — including type:'percent' ones computed on incomeTaxBase (1243). Every other take-home figure in the app is previewGross*keepRatio, and keepRatio = 1 - (federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview)/100 knows nothing about customWithholdings. Omitting the flat per-period deductions from a per-shift marginal figure is defensible; omitting a percent withholding is not — it is a per-dollar rate that applies fully at the margin. Reproduced with the extracted functions: base $50, fed 12, state 2.5, standard FICA, one custom withholding {Pension, 5, percent}, one 12h base shift in the period -> hero net 437.10 (Keep 73%), lab periodNet 437.10, Add-Shift previewNet 467 (implied keep 78%), day cell ~$467. Settings' goal line even claims to be 'the same per-shift take-home the Add-Shift preview uses' (4745-4746) — it is, and both are off from the hero. Hero and lab agree with each other; the preview family is the wrong one. (A related but separately-scoped omission was also raised: keepRatio also ignores flat pretax/posttax deductions the hero subtracts per paycheck, which is more defensible as a marginal-pricing choice once the paycheck already covers those flat amounts — the percent-withholding gap above has no such defense.)
failure: A nurse whose Settings carry a percent 'Other withholding' (e.g. a 5% 403b) logs one 12h day shift: the hero says $437 take-home this period and the lab says $437 / paycheck for a one-shift fortnight, but the Add-Shift sheet for that exact shift says 'about +$467 take-home', the calendar cell shows ~$467, and a $5,000 goal reads '≈ 11 typical 12h shifts' in Settings and in the preview when the hero's rate needs 12. Every pickup she evaluates is overstated by the withholding percentage.
fix: Fold the percent withholdings into keepRatio at 2820: const pctCW = (customWithholdings||[]).reduce((a,w)=> a + (w.type==='percent' ? (parseFloat(w.amount)||0) : 0), 0); const keepRatio = Math.max(0, 1 - (federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview+pctCW)/100). All five consumers then agree with computeNet at the margin. Add a harness assertion that, with a percent withholding set, Math.round(previewGross*keepRatio) === Math.round(computeNet(previewGross, taxInputs).net) when pretax/posttax are 0. Not an Invariant-3 function, but it changes displayed dollars, so run the wage-math probes and the deployed-build equality check.
dissent: The arithmetic is accurate but the failure path is not reachable through the shipped UI. `keepRatio` (index.html:2820) does omit `customWithholdings`, and `computeNet` (:1243) does subtract percent ones on `incomeTaxBase` — so IF state held a percent custom withholding, the Add-Shift preview (:4105), day cells (:3919/:3933), Settings goal line (:4747) and weekend-night card (:3434) would diverge from the hero/lab. But nothing in the app can put one there. `setCW` is invoked in exactly two places: `applyData` on load (:2318) and the clear-all reset to `[]` (:2338). It is passed into `SettingsSheet` as a prop (:3633/:4676) and never called — the Settings region (:4676–4800) contains no custom-withholding editor; the only "withholding" control is the FICA type/percent pair (:4731–4733). The paystub extractor (:3330–3400) maps a 403(b) line to `pretaxDeductions` (a flat dollar amount, which the finding itself concedes is defensibly excluded at the margin) and FICA to `ficaRate`; it never emits `customWithholdings`. Onboarding and the Add-Shift sheet don't touch it either. So the finding's scenario — "a nurse whose Settings carry a percent 'Other withholding' (e.g. a 5% 403b)" — names a control that does not exist; a real 403b lands in pretax dollars, not a percent withholding. The only routes to a non-empty `customWithholdings` are Import JSON (:4772 → `importData` :3074 → `applyData`) of a hand-edited file (the app's own export always carries `[]`), a direct localStorage/DB edit, or a legacy blob from a hypothetical earlier editor (pickaxe on the shallow 55-commit history finds none, and the 3 `user_data` rows are all builders). The finding's own repro was "with the extracted functions", i.e. synthetic state fed straight to the math, not the UI. Net: the whole `customWithholdings` feature is dormant (sanitized, priced by `computeNet`, shown as the $0 "Other withholdings" breakdown row at :3987, but with no input), so hero, lab and the preview family agree for every state the app can produce. At most a low note to fold percent withholdings into `keepRatio` if an editor ever ships — not a [high] displayed-dollar disagreement.
